newsitem.title: USA: German president tours Washington Holocaust museum.
newsitem.headline: German president tours Washington Holocaust museum.

text.p: German President Roman Herzog, who was a young boy during Adolf Hitler's rule, toured Washington's Holocaust museum on Wednesday and said he felt compassion for the victims but rage for the perpetrators.
Trailed by scores of dignitaries and reporters, he looked on solemnly as museum staff showed him disturbing, often graphic, scenes from the Holocaust in which six million Jews were killed.

"I feel deep compassion with the victims and a growing anger at what man can do to other men and to the reputation of the German people," Herzog, the first German president to visit the U.S. Holocaust Memorial Museum, told reporters.
"I feel strongly compelled to do everything I can to prevent something like this from ever happening in the future," he added after the one-hour visit.
Herzog, whose post is largely ceremonial, has in recent years taken on a role as Germany's moral conscience and devotes much public time to confronting Germany's Nazi past.

Aides said he had asked that reporters keep a "respectful distance" from him during his tour of the museum and on several occasions he gestured to security staff to keep back the throng of people following him.
After laying a wreath in the museum's hexagonal Hall of Remembrance, Herzog bowed his head and stood for a minute in silence in front of the eternal flame, which burns in memory of the dead.

Herzog walked onto a freight train that had taken deported Jews to their deaths in Treblinka camp in Poland and is one of the museum exhibits. Many people, especially the old, died on the railway cars even before they reached the camps.
Herzog was shown a model of the gas chambers in which prisoners were killed, and was led past thousands of pairs of shoes confiscated from people before they were sent into the chambers.
He told museum staff he believed such monuments were very important, especially for the young.
Germany is planning its own memorial to Jews murdered under Hitler's rule and there has been a public debate over what form the monument should take.
Herzog's museum tour was part of a three-day visit to the United States, during which he will also meet President Bill Clinton.
